label: accepted

evidence.V1: Low faceted slab with a moss top reads as a rock from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette; bottom origin, no visible floating of the main mass.
evidence.V2: Big mass plus a moss cap, but medium facets are few and large and the small pebble is only visible in the top view (hidden in front, three-quarter, silhouette, and not actually in frame in the pebble close-up).
evidence.V3: Partly stylised: the few big planar cuts make it read more like a cut gem/crystal than a weathered stone, and the 1-stud-tall slab is fairly flat.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistently softened edges catching a light line in the facets close-up.
evidence.V5: Facets close-up (studio and flat) shows a kinked step in the moss/stone colour boundary along the top edge (vertex-colour stair); facets otherwise shade cleanly.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values plus leaf-green moss as the single secondary; sandstone and basalt colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V7: 224 tris vs rock target 400 (ceiling 1000): under target.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, designed rock facets, stone + moss green per the Nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, bottom-centre origin.

evidence.V1: Reads as a moss-topped boulder from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette; the outline is a clean faceted chunk with no ambiguous protrusions.
evidence.V2: Big form plus about eight large medium-scale facets and a moss cap, but no small tier: the separate pebble seen in the top view is hidden in the front, three-quarter and silhouette views, and the pebble close-up frames empty space instead of it.
evidence.V3: The main mass is a low, wedge-like cut-gem block with few, very regular planes (front view is a flat lozenge); it reads as stylised but stiff, only partly exaggerated.
evidence.V4: Narrow chamfers on the facet edges catch a consistent light line in the studio close-up (close_facets_studio), matching the designed-facet rock treatment.
evidence.V5: Large flat facets shade cleanly with no pinches, seams or z-fighting; the only blemish is a small kink in the moss/stone colour boundary (close_facets_flat), which is a vertex-colour edge, not a shading artifact.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: stone grey in about three values plus a moss-green secondary; colourways (basalt, redrock) keep the same two-tone scheme.
evidence.V7: 224 tris against the rock target of 400 (ceiling 1000).
evidence.V8: Designed flat facets with chamfers, one vertex-colour material, stone hue + leaf-green secondary as the Nature kit specifies.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, white MeshPart.Color with vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Reads as a faceted boulder from front (low wedge), three-quarter (chunky polyhedron) and top; silhouette is a clean irregular heptagon with no confusing protrusions.
evidence.V2: Big form + moss cap give a clear primary/secondary split, but the small-scale read is weak: the pebble is only visible in the top view (detached behind the rock) and the pebble close-up frames empty space, so the third tier barely registers.
evidence.V3: Stylised low-poly boulder, but only ~1 stud tall against ~2.8 x 3.1 footprint so it reads as a flattened slab from the front; facet layout is fairly generic rather than a confident designed shape.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistent soft weighted-normal highlights along ridges (bright rim on front/close facets views); no razor or blobby edges.
evidence.V5: Close-up studio and flat views show clean planar facets, no pinches, seams or z-fighting; only a tiny step in the moss/stone colour boundary.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in 3 values plus one moss green secondary; colourways (basalt, sandstone) keep the same disciplined two-material split.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material, stone hue + moss secondary as specified for Nature, designed flat facets with soft normals: matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, CastShadow on, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre; A1-A18 pass.

artifacts: Kinked step in the moss/stone vertex-colour boundary on the top edge (facets close-up)
Satellite pebble only visible in the top view; pebble close-up shows empty space, so its placement and seating cannot be verified from the renders (no seats entry in the gate report)
Small kink in the moss/stone colour boundary on the front-left facet
Pebble close-up is framed on empty background; pebble not visible in front or three-quarter views (only in top view, separated behind main rock)
Small notch/step in the moss-to-stone boundary on the top edge
top_fixes: Move the pebble to a visible spot beside the rock (front/three-quarter side) and seat it, so the small tier reads; reframe the pebble close-up on it
Break the large gem-like planes with a few secondary bevelled cuts so it reads as weathered stone
Clean the moss boundary onto a straight edge loop and let the moss drape a little over the rim
Move the satellite pebble to the front/side next to the base so it reads in the main views, and add a seating check for it
Break up the regular cut-gem planes with one or two secondary bevelled facets or a chipped corner for a more confident stylised boulder
Let the moss cap creep down one facet with a softer, irregular edge instead of a straight band with a kink
Move or enlarge the pebble so it sits visibly at the base on the front/three-quarter side (and fix the pebble close-up framing)
Give the main rock more height or a stronger designed lean so the front view does not read as a flat slab
Clean the step in the moss boundary edge
